title: How can we change a triangle into a rectangle of equal area?
description: The Shulba Sutras ask for a method to change a triangle into a rectangle with the same area. Join the middles of the two slanting sides, cut off the top triangle, cut it down its height, and turn its two halves down into the gaps. The result is a rectangle on the same base with half the height.
teaching_notes: One idea: cutting and moving pieces keeps the area, and the pieces make a rectangle on the same base with half the height. Watch for children who think the rectangle keeps the full height.

video_script.why: The child sees that cutting a triangle and moving its pieces keeps the area, and that the pieces make a rectangle with the same base and half the height, matching half of base times height.
video_script.substitution: Join the middles of the two slanting sides, cut off the top triangle, split it down its height, and turn the two halves into the gaps.

maths_rules: triangle ABC with height AX on base BC; M and N are the midpoints of AB and AC; MN is parallel to BC at half the height
cut off the top triangle AMN and cut it along the height from A to MN, which meets MN at T, into two right triangles AMT and ANT
turn triangle AMT half way round about M: A goes to B and T goes to a point directly above B at height 1/2 AX; turn ANT the same way about N
the lower part BCNM and the two turned triangles make a rectangle with base BC and height 1/2 AX
area = BC × 1/2 AX = 1/2 × BC × AX, the area of the triangle
check with base 8 and height 6: triangle 1/2 × 8 × 6 = 24; rectangle 8 × 3 = 24
video_script.design: One idea: cutting and moving pieces keeps the area, and the pieces make a rectangle with half the height. The triangle stays on stage and the pieces move on it. The check uses base eight and height six.
open_questions: The worklist step says to drop perpendiculars from the two midpoints to the base and turn the two top triangles into the gap below. That description does not give a rectangle on the full base, so the video follows the working above: the top triangle is cut down its own height and its two halves are turned about the midpoints M and N. This should be checked against the book figure.
